record.original_question: Show that a classical open question in number theory, such as the Riemann hypothesis, is independent of the usual axioms of mathematics.

evidence.quote: Show that a classical open question in number theory, such as the Riemann hypothesis, is independent of the usual axioms. (I suspect that this is often the case, but that it cannot be proven.) (G. J. Chaitin)

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let ZFC denote Zermelo–Fraenkel set theory with the axiom of choice, regarded as the standard foundational axiom system for mathematics. The Riemann hypothesis (RH) is the assertion that every non-trivial zero of the Riemann zeta function $\zeta(s) = \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} n^{-s}$ (analytically continued to $\mathbb{C}\setminus\{1\}$) has real part equal to $1/2$. Equivalently, RH can be expressed as a $\Pi_1^0$ arithmetical statement about the integers.

Exhibit a classical open question in number theory — for instance, the Riemann hypothesis — and prove that it is independent of ZFC, i.e., that neither the statement nor its negation is provable from the axioms of ZFC (assuming ZFC is consistent). More precisely: produce a specific number-theoretic statement $\varphi$ (such as RH) that has been the object of classical study, together with a proof that ZFC $
vdash \varphi$ and ZFC $
vdash 
eg\varphi$.
artifact.status_search_result: No proof of the independence of the Riemann hypothesis (or any comparable classical number-theoretic conjecture) from ZFC is known. RH remains an open problem, and its logical status with respect to ZFC is also unresolved; this is a long-standing speculation associated with Chaitin's algorithmic information theory perspective.

status_evidence.title: Riemann hypothesis - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: The Riemann hypothesis remains one of the most famous open problems in mathematics; it has neither been proved nor disproved.
status_evidence.claim: RH is still open, with no known independence result.

status_evidence.title: Chaitin, 'Thoughts on the Riemann Hypothesis'
status_evidence.snippet: Chaitin speculates that RH might be undecidable but provides no proof of independence from ZFC.
status_evidence.claim: The independence of RH from ZFC is a conjecture, not a theorem.
